reader_question: What does the first page of a law tell a reader?
grade_line: Documented: Public Law 119-12’s first page, as the Government Publishing Office prints it
title: The first page of Public Law 119-12 gives its number, the Congress that passed it, where it starts in the Statutes at Large, the day it was approved and the bill it began as.
measure_line: The parts of the first page of Public Law 119-12, the TAKE IT DOWN Act, redrawn with the page’s own words
notes: The drawing stops after section 1; section 2 begins lower on the same page.
The page prints a dash between the law’s number and its date in the running head; the drawing sets it as a rule.
alt: A drawing of the first page of Public Law 119-12 with its eleven parts numbered, from the running head and the law’s number at the top to the short title section and the two notes in its margin.

table.caption: The parts of the first page of Public Law 119-12, in reading order

chart_notes: Each numbered square marks a part of the page; the list beside the page names each part and what it tells a reader, in the same order.
phone_note: Under 600 px the list of parts follows the page; where the page’s margin column cannot hold its words, the margin’s parts follow the lines they sit beside, set flush right.
notes_internal: Infographics maker, round 4. Data plan row 125 (data lead change 2), rule 14.139. Domain D04 from the sidecar.

Every word the page drawing prints is a row's printed_text, split only where the page breaks a line; the running head's three pieces are the row's semicolon-separated parts, joined as the page joins them, with a rule one em wide for the page's dash (DR-79's drawing of an em dash).
Layout checked against the page itself: govinfo PLAW-119publ12.pdf, page 1, fetched November 13, 2026 to the maker's scratch, rendered and read with pdftotext -layout.

Row 11, the margin short title, added by the research lead (IM-4), sits above row 10 in the margin; the parts are numbered in the order they sit on the page (the sort puts 11 before 10), so the drawing and the list print 10 for row 11 and 11 for row 10, and the table's Number column maps them the same way.
Source line: the sidecar's date_on_page variant (IM-3); grade line as ruling (c); the approval date prints only on the page drawing and its callout.
Data lead (20:59 UTC) accepted numbered markers with no leader lines, and the redraw in Inter with the drawing's own line breaks.
source_line: Source: Public Law 119-12, the TAKE IT DOWN Act, 139 Stat. 55, first page, United States, from govinfo, U.S. Government Publishing Office. Retrieved November 12, 2026.
